label: November 1917
headline: Bells for Cambrai
deck: Tanks break the Hindenburg Line; ten days later the Germans strike back
caption: A tank carrying a bundle of brushwood crosses a wide trench at Cambrai
body: For the first time in the war, church bells ring across Britain for a victory. At Cambrai on 20 November nearly four hundred tanks, followed by infantry and with no long bombardment to warn the enemy, have broken through the Hindenburg Line on a front of six miles.

The success does not last. Tanks break down, the cavalry cannot get forward, and Bourlon Wood is fought over for a week. On 30 November German divisions, with short bombardments and infiltrating storm troops, attack the flanks of the bulge and win back most of the ground.
Allied leaders meeting at Rapallo on 7 November set up a Supreme War Council to direct the war together.
In Palestine the British advance on Jerusalem after the fall of Gaza, and take the port of Jaffa on 16 November.
briefs: Lord Lansdowne's letter calls for a negotiated peace
The Bolsheviks publish the Allies' secret treaties
Lettow-Vorbeck's force crosses into Portuguese East Africa
